tools.name: analytics_query
tools.title: Query analytics
tools.triggerDescription: Returns time series for named datasets (datasets[]) such as rowsSyncedByTime, ingestionLag, readerLag, rowLag and flushTime over from/to (RFC3339). Pass pipelineUUID from pipeline_list to scope to one pipeline; it is required for environment-scoped keys. Total lag is readerLag plus ingestionLag at each timestamp. Use for lag or throughput over time. For one per-table lag number and row count, use pipeline_usage.

tools.name: column_hashing_salt_delete
tools.title: Delete a column hashing salt
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes a column hashing salt by UUID. Does not unhash already-landed columns.

tools.name: column_hashing_salt_list
tools.title: List column hashing salts
tools.triggerDescription: Lists column hashing salt names and UUIDs (no secret).

tools.name: column_hashing_salt_preview
tools.title: Preview a column hashing salt
tools.triggerDescription: Hashes a sample string with this salt and returns the hex digest.

tools.name: column_hashing_salt_update
tools.title: Update a column hashing salt
tools.triggerDescription: Updates the name and description of an existing column hashing salt. Does not rotate the secret.

tools.name: company_trigger_automatic_schema_changes
tools.title: Trigger automatic schema changes for a company
tools.triggerDescription: Enqueues automatic schema changes for all eligible running pipelines. For one pipeline, use pipeline_trigger_automatic_schema_changes.

tools.name: connector_create
tools.title: Create a connector
tools.triggerDescription: Creates a saved source or destination connector. Pass type, label, and sharedConfig (host, user, password, and type-specific fields). Keep the returned UUID for pipeline_create_from_source.

tools.name: connector_delete
tools.title: Delete a connector
tools.triggerDescription: Permanently deletes a saved connector by UUID and stops pipelines that depend on it.

tools.name: connector_detail
tools.title: Get a saved connector
tools.triggerDescription: Returns a saved connector by uuid from connector_list, not a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID. Includes type, label, and sharedConfig. Sensitive fields may be masked placeholders. With connectors:write, you can ping that connector by passing this payload into unsaved_connector_ping with uuid set so stored secrets unmask.

tools.name: connector_drop_postgres_replication_slot
tools.title: Drop a PostgreSQL replication slot
tools.triggerDescription: Drops an inactive PostgreSQL replication slot. Check connector_fetch_postgres_replication_slots first: only an inactive or lost slot can be dropped.

tools.name: connector_fetch_databases
tools.title: Fetch databases for a saved connector
tools.triggerDescription: Lists database names a saved source can see. uuid must come from connector_list with includeSourceConnectors=true. Do not pass a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID.

tools.name: connector_fetch_postgres_replication_slots
tools.title: List PostgreSQL replication slots
tools.triggerDescription: Lists replication slots on a saved Postgres source (name, database, active, walStatus, retainedWALBytes, isReplica). uuid must come from connector_list with includeSourceConnectors=true, not a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID; pass databaseName for the pipeline's reader database. Use for slot health and WAL retention, and to confirm a slot is inactive before connector_drop_postgres_replication_slot.

tools.name: connector_fetch_postgres_settings
tools.title: Fetch PostgreSQL settings
tools.triggerDescription: Returns replication-relevant server settings (name, value, unit, category) for a saved Postgres source, such as wal_level, max_replication_slots, max_wal_senders, and max_slot_wal_keep_size. uuid must come from connector_list with includeSourceConnectors=true. Use to check CDC prerequisites (wal_level must be logical) before pipeline_start or after it fails. Settings are changed on the database, not through Artie.

tools.name: connector_fetch_schemas
tools.title: Fetch schemas for a saved connector
tools.triggerDescription: Lists schemas on a saved connector. uuid must come from connector_list. Do not pass a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID. Pass schemaName into connector_fetch_tables when the destination requires it.

tools.name: connector_fetch_table_detail
tools.title: Fetch table detail for a saved connector
tools.triggerDescription: Returns columns and metadata for one table on a saved connector. uuid must come from connector_list (includeSourceConnectors=true for sources). Do not pass a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID. tableName is required. This is column metadata, not pipeline lag or row counts.

tools.name: connector_fetch_tables
tools.title: Fetch tables for a saved connector
tools.triggerDescription: Lists tables on a saved connector. uuid must come from connector_list. Do not pass a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID. Use to choose names for pipeline_update.tables.

tools.name: connector_generate_shadow_script
tools.title: Generate Oracle shadow table script
tools.triggerDescription: Returns SQL to create Oracle shadow tables for CDC. Oracle sources only.

tools.name: connector_list
tools.title: List connectors
tools.triggerDescription: Lists saved connectors. Defaults to destinations; pass includeSourceConnectors=true for sources. Call this before connector_fetch_databases, connector_fetch_schemas, connector_fetch_tables, or connector_fetch_table_detail — those tools need a uuid from this list, not a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID from pipeline_list.

tools.name: connector_start_dynamo_db_export
tools.title: Start a DynamoDB export
tools.triggerDescription: Starts a DynamoDB point-in-time export. DynamoDB sources only; for SQL CDC use pipeline_start.

tools.name: data_catalog_search
tools.title: Search the data catalog
tools.triggerDescription: Searches ingested catalog metadata. For live source tables, use connector_fetch_tables.

tools.name: encryption_key_delete
tools.title: Delete an encryption key
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes an encryption key by UUID. Does not decrypt already-landed columns.

tools.name: encryption_key_list
tools.title: List encryption keys
tools.triggerDescription: Lists encryption key names and UUIDs (no secret material).

tools.name: encryption_key_update
tools.title: Update an encryption key
tools.triggerDescription: Updates the name and description of an existing encryption key. Does not rotate the key material.

tools.name: ingestion_api_key_delete
tools.title: Delete an ingestion API key
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes an ingestion API key by UUID.

tools.name: ingestion_api_key_update
tools.title: Update an ingestion API key
tools.triggerDescription: Updates metadata on an existing ingestion API key. Does not mint a new key.

tools.name: kafka_admin_user_delete
tools.title: Delete an admin Kafka user
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes an admin Kafka user on a BYOC cluster. Kafka revokes its access within seconds, so clients using it stop working. userUUID comes from kafka_user_list where accessProfile is admin. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_admin_user_detail
tools.title: Get an admin Kafka user
tools.triggerDescription: One admin Kafka user on a BYOC cluster, without its password. There is no admin user list: find the userUUID in kafka_user_list where accessProfile is admin.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_detail
tools.title: Get a Kafka cluster
tools.triggerDescription: Gets one Kafka cluster by the uuid from kafka_cluster_list. For a Managed cluster it also returns the cluster's saved configuration; for a BYOC cluster it matches its kafka_cluster_list entry.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_list
tools.title: List Kafka clusters
tools.triggerDescription: Start here for any Kafka question: lists the company's Kafka clusters with uuid, name, status and isManaged. Every other kafka_* tool takes that uuid. isManaged decides which tools work: Managed clusters use kafka_managed_user_*, kafka_cluster_rates and kafka_consumer_group_details; BYOC clusters (isManaged false) use kafka_user_*, kafka_admin_user_* and kafka_cluster_settings.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_metrics_graph
tools.title: Get Kafka metrics graphs
tools.triggerDescription: Broker, topic and partition metrics and per-broker CPU over time, between from and to, for a Strimzi cluster. Use for trends and CPU questions; for current throughput and consumer lag on a Managed cluster, kafka_cluster_rates is quicker.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_rates
tools.title: Get Managed Kafka cluster rates
tools.triggerDescription: Managed clusters only, and the cluster must be active (400 or 409 otherwise). Shows current messages in and bytes out per second, each topic's message rate, and each consumer group's lag per topic over range (1h or 6h). Use first for whether a Managed cluster is busy or any consumer is behind.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_settings
tools.title: Get a BYOC Kafka cluster's settings
tools.triggerDescription: BYOC Strimzi clusters only: Kafka version, broker count, and disk size and storage class per broker. Managed and MSK clusters return supported false; for a Managed cluster's configuration use kafka_cluster_detail.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_storage_graph
tools.title: Get Kafka storage graph
tools.triggerDescription: Broker disk usage over time, between from and to. Use for whether the disk is filling up; follow with kafka_topic_sizes to see which topics use the space.

tools.name: kafka_cluster_summary
tools.title: Get Kafka cluster summary
tools.triggerDescription: Returns only two counts for a cluster: topics and consumer groups. For status or configuration use kafka_cluster_detail.

tools.name: kafka_consumer_group_detail
tools.title: Get Kafka consumer group detail
tools.triggerDescription: One consumer group's members and per-topic offset lag, on any cluster type. Use for whether a specific consumer is behind. groupID comes from kafka_consumer_group_list.

tools.name: kafka_consumer_group_details
tools.title: Get every Kafka consumer group's detail
tools.triggerDescription: Managed clusters only (400 otherwise): every consumer group's members and per-topic offset lag in one call. Use instead of calling kafka_consumer_group_detail once per group.

tools.name: kafka_consumer_group_list
tools.title: List Kafka consumer groups
tools.triggerDescription: Lists consumer group IDs on a cluster, without lag. groupID is what kafka_consumer_group_detail takes. For lag on every group of a Managed cluster in one call, use kafka_consumer_group_details instead.

tools.name: kafka_managed_user_delete
tools.title: Delete a Managed Kafka cluster's user
tools.triggerDescription: Managed clusters only: deletes a login. Kafka rejects its password within seconds, so clients using it stop working. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_managed_user_list
tools.title: List a Managed Kafka cluster's users
tools.triggerDescription: Managed clusters only: lists the cluster's extra Kafka logins with their ACLs, without passwords. userUUID is what kafka_managed_user_update and kafka_managed_user_delete take.

tools.name: kafka_managed_user_update
tools.title: Change a Managed Kafka cluster's user's ACLs
tools.triggerDescription: Managed clusters only: replaces a login's ACLs with the acls you send, so any ACL left out is removed. The password stays the same. Read the current ACLs with kafka_managed_user_list and confirm the change with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_create
tools.title: Create a Kafka topic
tools.triggerDescription: Creates a topic with topic, partitionCount, replicationFactor and optional configEntries. On a BYOC cluster the name must start with <companyUUID>.customer.; on a Managed cluster any name works except the cluster's own (__ and strimzi.cruisecontrol.*), and the cluster must be active. Confirm the settings with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_delete
tools.title: Delete a Kafka topic
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes a topic and every message in it; this can't be undone. Don't delete a topic with artieManaged true (it feeds Artie pipelines) unless the user asked for that exact topic. Confirm the topic name with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_detail
tools.title: Get Kafka topic detail
tools.triggerDescription: One topic's per-partition sizes, replication, leaders and offsets, plus the Artie pipelines (names and uuids) that read it. topic comes from kafka_topic_list. Use before changing or deleting a topic to see what depends on it.

tools.name: kafka_topic_latest_message
tools.title: Get latest Kafka topic message
tools.triggerDescription: Returns the contents of the newest message on partition 0 of a topic. It can be customer data, so call it only when the user asks to see a message, and quote no more than needed. Fails unless the company allows reading Kafka messages.

tools.name: kafka_topic_list
tools.title: List Kafka topics
tools.triggerDescription: Lists a cluster's topics with partitionCount, retention, tiered storage and artieManaged. artieManaged true means the topic carries Artie CDC data that pipelines read. The topic name is the topic other topic tools take. Cached for 2 minutes; pass forceRefresh after creating a topic.

tools.name: kafka_topic_partitions_increase
tools.title: Increase Kafka topic partitions
tools.triggerDescription: Adds partitions to a topic; this can't be undone and changes which partition each key lands on. Refused on artieManaged topics. Send currentPartitionCount from kafka_topic_list and the new total as newPartitionCount. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_retention_update
tools.title: Change Kafka topic retention
tools.triggerDescription: Sets only a topic's retention.ms. Prefer kafka_topic_settings_update, which also handles local retention and tiered storage. Shorter retention deletes older messages for good. Confirm the change with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_settings_update
tools.title: Change Kafka topic settings
tools.triggerDescription: Changes a topic's retentionMS, localRetentionMS and tieredStorage; send only what changes. Shorter retention deletes older messages for good, and on an artieManaged topic can drop change events before pipelines read them. Confirm the change with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_topic_sizes
tools.title: Get Kafka topic partition sizes
tools.triggerDescription: Bytes used by every topic on a cluster, per partition, in one call. Use to find which topics fill the disk. Cached unless forceRefresh is true.

tools.name: kafka_user_delete
tools.title: Delete a Kafka user
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes a producer_consumer Kafka user on a BYOC cluster. Kafka revokes its access within seconds, so clients using it stop working. userUUID comes from kafka_user_list. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: kafka_user_detail
tools.title: Get a Kafka user
tools.triggerDescription: One producer_consumer Kafka user on a BYOC cluster, without its password. userUUID comes from kafka_user_list. Passwords aren't available through MCP; the user can copy one from the Artie dashboard.

tools.name: kafka_user_list
tools.title: List Kafka users
tools.triggerDescription: BYOC clusters only; Managed clusters return 400, so use kafka_managed_user_list there. Lists Kafka users of both access profiles, without passwords. accessProfile picks the tools for a user: producer_consumer uses kafka_user_detail and kafka_user_delete, admin uses kafka_admin_user_detail and kafka_admin_user_delete.

tools.name: pipeline_backfill_tables
tools.title: Backfill pipeline tables
tools.triggerDescription: Backfills tables already on a running pipeline by table UUID from pipeline_detail (not connector_fetch_tables). To attach tables, use pipeline_update.

tools.name: pipeline_cancel_backfill_tables
tools.title: Cancel backfill
tools.triggerDescription: Cancels an in-progress backfill for the given table UUIDs.

tools.name: pipeline_create
tools.title: Create a pipeline on an existing source reader
tools.triggerDescription: Attaches a new pipeline to an existing sourceReaderUUID. The reader must be unused or already shared (fan-out: one CDC capture, many destinations). To start a new capture from a source connector, use pipeline_create_from_source.

tools.name: pipeline_create_from_source
tools.title: Create a new pipeline from a source
tools.triggerDescription: Creates a draft pipeline plus a new dedicated (non-shared) source reader. Pass sourceConnectorUUID to reuse a saved source; sourceType alone inserts an empty connector. For Postgres, Cockroach, and Oracle, pass database (from connector_fetch_databases) so the new reader can start. For a second destination on the same capture, use pipeline_create on a shared reader.

tools.name: pipeline_delete
tools.title: Delete pipeline
tools.triggerDescription: Permanently deletes a pipeline by UUID. Does not delete connectors.

tools.name: pipeline_detail
tools.title: Get pipeline configuration
tools.triggerDescription: Returns FullPipeline for a uuid from pipeline_list: tables (uuid, name, schema, status), destinationUUID, specificDestCfg, and sourceReaderUUID. Echo this into pipeline_update; do not send pipeline_list. Use for per-table status and backfill table UUIDs. sourceReaderUUID is the uuid for source_reader_detail and source_reader_update, not a connector uuid. This is not lag (pipeline_usage) or error logs (pipeline_error_logs). Omit includeRelatedObjects — that Dashboard flag wraps connectors and is not this tool's success shape.

tools.name: pipeline_detect_schema_changes
tools.title: Detect schema changes
tools.triggerDescription: Checks the source for table or schema drift. To apply destination DDL, use pipeline_trigger_automatic_schema_changes.

tools.name: pipeline_error_logs
tools.title: List pipeline error logs
tools.triggerDescription: Returns recent error logs for a saved pipeline (message, errorDetail, table/schema, timestamps). Pass the pipeline uuid from pipeline_list. Use when the user asks why a pipeline failed or is unhealthy. This is not lag (pipeline_usage), per-table status (pipeline_detail), or replication slot size.

tools.name: pipeline_list
tools.title: List pipelines
tools.triggerDescription: Lists pipelines with uuid, name, and status. This is not a full configuration — do not send it to pipeline_update. Full config, per-table status, and table UUIDs are pipeline_detail. Failure messages are pipeline_error_logs, not status. sourceReaderUUID is not a connector id; call connector_list before connector_fetch_table_detail or other connector_fetch_* tools.

tools.name: pipeline_start
tools.title: Start pipeline
tools.triggerDescription: Deploys a draft or resumes a paused pipeline once destination, tables, and (Postgres/Cockroach/Oracle) reader database are set. Do not call immediately after create-from-source. If start 400s that two source readers share replication slot artie, GET source_reader_detail for sourceReaderUUID from pipeline_detail, set settings.replicationSlotOverride to a unique name, POST source_reader_update with the echoed reader, then retry start.

tools.name: pipeline_trigger_automatic_schema_changes
tools.title: Trigger automatic schema changes for a pipeline
tools.triggerDescription: Applies detected source DDL on one pipeline. For every eligible pipeline, use company_trigger_automatic_schema_changes.

tools.name: pipeline_update
tools.title: Update pipeline
tools.triggerDescription: Replaces the full pipeline configuration (not a PATCH). Echo the last FullPipeline from pipeline_create_from_source, pipeline_update, or pipeline_detail — not pipeline_list — and send destinationUUID and tables together; a destination-only body is rejected and omitting tables deletes all tables.

tools.name: pipeline_update_status
tools.title: Update pipeline status
tools.triggerDescription: Pauses or resumes an already-configured pipeline. For first deploy, use pipeline_start.

tools.name: pipeline_usage
tools.title: Get pipeline usage
tools.triggerDescription: Returns per-table ingestion lag and row counts for a saved pipeline over a time range. Pass the pipeline uuid plus from and to as RFC3339 timestamps; set excludeBackfills=true to leave backfill rows out of row counts. Use when the user asks about lag, throughput, or rows processed. This is not slot health, warehouse correctness, pipeline_list status, pipeline_detail table status, or error logs (pipeline_error_logs).

tools.name: private_link_connection_create
tools.title: Create a PrivateLink connection
tools.triggerDescription: Creates a PrivateLink connection: pass vpcServiceName and availabilityZoneIds for an AWS data plane, or privateLinkServiceAlias for an Azure one. Keep the returned UUID; there is no list tool.

tools.name: private_link_connection_delete
tools.title: Delete a PrivateLink connection
tools.triggerDescription: Permanently deletes a PrivateLink connection by UUID.

tools.name: private_link_connection_detail
tools.title: Get a PrivateLink connection
tools.triggerDescription: Returns one PrivateLink connection by UUID.

tools.name: private_link_connection_update
tools.title: Update a PrivateLink connection
tools.triggerDescription: Updates a PrivateLink connection. The data plane and Private Link target (VPC service name and AZs on AWS, privateLinkServiceAlias on Azure) are only mutable while under review or errored.

tools.name: snowflake_eco_schedule_create
tools.title: Create a Snowflake Eco Mode schedule
tools.triggerDescription: Creates a schedule of peak hours (time zone, days, start and end time). Outside them, attached pipelines use its off-peak flush rules.

tools.name: snowflake_eco_schedule_delete
tools.title: Delete a Snowflake Eco Mode schedule
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes a Snowflake Eco Mode schedule that no pipeline uses.

tools.name: snowflake_eco_schedule_detail
tools.title: Get a Snowflake Eco Mode schedule
tools.triggerDescription: Returns one Snowflake Eco Mode schedule by UUID.

tools.name: snowflake_eco_schedule_list
tools.title: List Snowflake Eco Mode schedules
tools.triggerDescription: Lists the company's Snowflake Eco Mode schedules. Use a schedule's uuid as snowflakeEcoScheduleUUID on a pipeline update.

tools.name: snowflake_eco_schedule_update
tools.title: Update a Snowflake Eco Mode schedule
tools.triggerDescription: Replaces a schedule's name and settings.

tools.name: source_reader_delete
tools.title: Delete a source reader
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes a source reader unused by any active pipeline. Does not delete the source connector.

tools.name: source_reader_deploy
tools.title: Deploy a source reader
tools.triggerDescription: Deploys a shared, validated source reader. To take a draft pipeline live, use pipeline_start.

tools.name: source_reader_detail
tools.title: Get a source reader
tools.triggerDescription: Returns a source reader by uuid from pipeline_detail.sourceReaderUUID, not a pipeline uuid or connector uuid. Includes database, tablesConfig, and settings (replicationSlotOverride, publicationNameOverride, heartbeats). Sensitive fields may be present. Echo this into source_reader_update; do not invent a partial body. If pipeline_start 400s that two readers share slot artie, GET this, set settings.replicationSlotOverride to a unique lowercase name (digits and underscores, <=63), POST source_reader_update, then retry start.

tools.name: source_reader_update
tools.title: Update a source reader
tools.triggerDescription: Applies a SourceReader from source_reader_detail. Echo the last GET and change only the intended fields. Omitting name, database, or connectorUUID blanks them. To fix a duplicate Postgres slot (pipeline_start 400 that two readers share artie), set settings.replicationSlotOverride to a unique lowercase name, then pipeline_start. This is not pipeline_update or connector_update.

tools.name: ssh_tunnel_create
tools.title: Create an SSH tunnel
tools.triggerDescription: Creates an SSH tunnel record. Keep the returned UUID; there is no list tool.

tools.name: ssh_tunnel_delete
tools.title: Delete an SSH tunnel
tools.triggerDescription: Deletes an SSH tunnel unused by any connector or pipeline.

tools.name: ssh_tunnel_detail
tools.title: Get an SSH tunnel
tools.triggerDescription: Returns one SSH tunnel by UUID (no private key).

tools.name: ssh_tunnel_update
tools.title: Update an SSH tunnel
tools.triggerDescription: Updates name, host, port, or username on an existing SSH tunnel. Does not rotate keys.

tools.name: unsaved_connector_ping
tools.title: Ping a connector
tools.triggerDescription: Pings a connector before connector_create. Pass type, sharedConfig (host, user, password, and type-specific fields), and connectionRole (source or destination). This is not a uuid ping — do not pass a pipeline uuid or sourceReaderUUID. Postgres needs a database name, Oracle a service name, S3 a bucket. Success is {"success": true}. A 422 error means the connection failed (unreachable host, bad credentials, missing permissions) and its message says why; a 400 means the request itself is invalid.
